content:
Facts: Daughter sued brother and mother challenging 2003 holographic will as apocryphal; joined forgery-complaint proceedings established will-falsity; plaintiff sought unworthiness declaration against brother who admitted drafting false will claiming mutual family-agreement corresponding to father's actual wishes to avoid intestacy; brother counterclaimed sister's unworthiness; plaintiff sought reduction of earlier 1989 public will; defendant mother died during proceedings.
Legal Framework: Articles 463(6), 591(3), 602, 606 Italian Civil Code (unworthiness for false-will creation/use; testamentary incapacity; holographic validity; nullity); Art. 2946 Civil Code (ordinary limitation period); Arts. 183(6), 190 CPC (assertive/evidentiary preclusions); case law on unworthiness-action nature (Cass. 3171/1962, 2145/1974, 7266/2006, 24252/2016).
Interpretive Issues: Unworthiness-action limitation period commencement (succession-opening versus knowledge-of-falsity date); burden allocation proving absence of offending-deceased-will intent when false-will drafter admits creation; evidentiary requirements proving false-will correspondence to actual testator-wishes; admissibility of facts/evidence introduced post-assertive-preclusions; reduction-action requirements proving real-property ownership; effect of mother's death on interruption when death communicated by other-party counsel not deceased's attorney.
Principles Applied: Interruption-declaration requires death-communication by deceased-party's attorney, not other-party counsel. Joined forgery-proceedings established 2003 will material-falsity; will entire-destruction ordered. Negative-origin-assessment burden lies with contesting-party per general negative-verification principles. Expert-analysis established will non-autograph. Art. 463(6) excludes from succession as unworthy anyone drawing-up false-will or using it. False-will creation/conscious-use constitutes unworthiness-grounds unless unworthy-person proves non-intent offending deceased-will because: (a) provision-content corresponds to testator-will; (b) deceased consented to form-completion by drafter if personally-unable, firmly-intending avoiding intestate-succession. Defendant admitted drafting 2003 will albeit claiming mutual family-agreement with mother/sister. Defendant published will 15/07/2005, used it for succession-declaration. No evidence proving: (a) 2003 disposition-correspondence to testator-wishes; (b) deceased's consent to son-drafting. Requested investigative-measures not aimed proving deceased-wishes/consent but mutual mother-children agreement. Evidence suggests different wishes: beneficiary/object discrepancies between 1989 will (beneficiaries: son/wife; objects: Amoruso-land, half-apartment) versus 2003 will (beneficiaries: wife/son/daughter; objects: different-land, half-apartment, daughter's-bare-ownership with wife-usufruct). Unworthiness declared; failure proving false-will reflected actual-wishes/deceased-consent. Unworthiness configured as civil-sanction not preventing inheritance-acquisition but causing succession-exclusion requiring constitutive-judgment upon interested-party request; prevailing-opinion subjects action to ordinary Art. 2946 limitation-period running from succession-opening (not imprescriptible). Counterclaim time-barred: succession opened 26/03/2005, counterclaim filed 16/06/2015 (ten-years expired). Alternative case-law (Cass. 7266/2006) excludes succession-opening as automatic limitation-commencement when entitled-person lacks reasonable-certainty based on clear objective-indicators; contra non valentem principle requires protection; Art. 2935 references legal-possibility (not factual-impediments including blameless-ignorance); limitation begins when reasonable-certainty/awareness exists regarding: (a) party claiming heir-status via presumed-false will; (b) own inheritance-right via objectively-unambiguous indicators determinable by normal-diligence person. Even under alternative-approach, claim time-barred; prolonged-inaction unjustified; ignorance not blameless when drafter admitted self-drafting thus knowing proven-falsity/prejudice. Evidence inadmissible: facts introduced post-assertive-preclusions expiring at Art. 183(6)(1) brief; defendant filed no such brief; second-preliminary-brief facts (2005-meetings, father-informing-family, mother's-amendment-request, Revenue-Agency-meeting, witnesses-present-during-drafting) never alleged before preclusions-expiry. Strict-preclusions system (Law 353/1990, reinforced 263/1995, 69/2009): evidence-right exercisable only regarding promptly-alleged facts before assertive-preclusions; ordinary-proceedings assertive-preclusions mature before evidentiary-preclusions unlike labor-proceedings. Evidence-request timely-formulated becomes inadmissible when referencing never-raised facts. Proven circumstances wouldn't postpone limitation-commencement given vague time-reference ("mid-June 2005") precluding certain false-will-drafting date. Ignorance non-blameless; commencement not postponable past succession-opening. Reduction-claim unfounded: petitory-nature judgments (division, reduction with legitimate-infringement, petitio hereditatis) based on co-ownership/real-right requiring ascertainment; parties must prove co-ownership via written-deed ad substantiam or equivalent-fact (adverse-possession), not cadastral-certificates (subsidiary boundary-elements), alleged-acknowledgments, or deductive-process. No ownership-proof documents produced: neither origin-titles (deceased's property-purchase never-mentioned) nor Land-Registry inspections. Required: title-deeds, notarial-certificate/Land-Registry-issued indicating transcriptions favor/against from purchase-date until succession-opening, against-successors from opening until claim-transcription/proceedings-establishment; verifying property-deceased-ownership then party-ownership at proceedings-establishment. Risk: pending-decision property-sales to third-parties if claim untranscribed (present-case); considerable years since presumed-purchase. Documentation essential ascertaining other joint-creditors/participant-assignees per Art. 1113, 784 CPC; intervention verifying transactions-correctness preventing guarantee-reduction. Documentation-absence precludes reduction-grant; Court lacks ownership-knowledge. Burden-proof per Art. 2697: absent documentation, no reduction-orderable. Unworthiness-ruling requires asset-return to estate; plaintiff/mother possess co-ownership-right over assets bequeathed to unworthy proportional to legitimate-succession shares. Pro-rata restitution rejected absent division-claim; assets belong indiscriminately to heirs until joint-ownership dissolution-request. Fruits-restitution rejected: no proof fruits-existence from joint-inheritance assets; regulation occurs at division-time. Damages rejected: plaintiff limited itself general compensation-request without damage-allegation; failed offering evidence proving non-contractual tort-elements (harmful-conduct, damage-existence/extent). Donation/sale-nullity claims rejected: no nullity-grounds alleged/proven; mother's donation disposing her-rights unrelated to testamentary-dispositions/inheritance; sale-contract valid dispositive-act concerning unrelated-rights freely-entered.
